chunks: And by this chain, from Aban, from Uqba ibn Bashir al-Asadi, from al-Kumayt ibn Zayd al-Asadi, who said:

I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and he said: 'By Allah, O Kumayt, if we had wealth, we would have given you from it, but for you is what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Hassan ibn Thabit: 'The Holy Spirit will not cease to be with you as long as you defend us'.
I said, 'Inform me about the two men.'

He took the pillow and pressed it against his chest, then said: 'By Allah, O Kumayt, no cupping vessel has spilled blood, nor wealth taken unlawfully, nor a stone turned from another stone, except that it is upon their necks.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about the deeds of Abu Bakr and Umar?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) bestows upon the poet Al-Kumayt the spiritual reward of *Hassan ibn Thabit*, linking his poetic defense of the Ahl al-Bayt to the divine inspiration of the Holy Spirit. The Imam’s gesture of breaking the cushion against his chest while naming Abu Bakr and Umar signifies that the cumulative weight of their specific actions—shedding blood, appropriating wealth, and displacing authority—is metaphorically borne upon their necks, a key motif in Shia eschatology.

en.hubeali: H 14523 – And by this chain, from Abaan, from Uqba Bin Basheer Al-Asady, from Al-Kumeyt Bin Zayd Al-asady who said:

‘I came up to Abu Ja’farasws, so heasws said: ‘By Allahazwj, O Kumeyt, if weasws had in ourasws possession some wealth, weasws would have given you from it, but for you is what the Rasoolsaww Allahazwj said to Hassan Bin Sabit: ‘The Holy Spirit will not cease to be with you so long as you defend ussaww’.
I said, ‘Inform me about the two men (Abu Bakr and Umar)’.

He (the narrator) said: ‘He<sup>asws</sup> took the pillow and folded it unto his<sup>asws</sup> chest’ and said: ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, O Kumeyt, there is no blood spilled unlawfully, nor any wealth taken without right, and not stone turned from another stone except that it would be upon their necks’.
